report_name: N-able Confirms Server Breach Caused Email Security Service Outage

identities.name: N-able
identities.description: A managed service provider (MSP) infrastructure company that suffered a security breach affecting its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud email security products. The breach resulted in a multi-day service disruption.

infrastructure.name: Compromised N-able Cloud Server
infrastructure.description: A server in the shared cloud environment supporting Mail Assure and SpamExperts that was subject to unauthorized access, leading to the disabling of management portals and APIs.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Management Infrastructure Logins
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cloud Management Infrastructure Logins
id: 7b3d9c1a-0f5e-4b9a-8c7d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Monitors for anomalous API calls or logins to cloud management infrastructure from unusual IP ranges or user agents, which could indicate a compromise similar to the N-able incident.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-confirms-hackers-accessed-cloud.html
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
level: medium
logsource:
  category: cloud
  service: audit
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: 'signin.amazonaws.com'
    eventName: 'ConsoleLogin'
    responseElements.ConsoleLogin: 'Failure'
  timeframe: 10m
  condition: selection | count() > 10
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate users with password issues.
  - Application misconfigurations.
indicators.description: This rule detects multiple failed login attempts to a cloud management console, which could indicate brute-force or credential stuffing attacks against management infrastructure, as suggested in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Unexpected Data Egress from Management Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Unexpected Data Egress from Management Server
id: 8c4e0d2b-1a6f-4c0b-9d8e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
status: experimental
description: Detects unusually large data transfers from management servers to external IP addresses, which could indicate data exfiltration.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-confirms-hackers-accessed-cloud.html
tags:
  - attack.t1041
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    SourceIp: 
      - '10.0.1.5' # Replace with actual management server IPs
      - '192.168.1.10'
    DestinationIp|private: false
    SentBytes|gt: 10000000 # 10 MB
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large data transfers, such as backups or software updates.
indicators.description: This rule detects large, unexpected data transfers from management servers to external addresses, which could be a sign of data exfiltration following a compromise.

indicators.name: Brute-Force Attempts on Management Interfaces
indicators.pattern:
title: Brute-Force Attempts on Management Interfaces
id: 9d5f1e3c-2b7a-4d1c-ae9f-3a4b5c6d7e8f
status: experimental
description: Detects multiple failed login attempts, which could indicate a brute-force attack against administrative interfaces.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-confirms-hackers-accessed-cloud.html
tags:
  - attack.t1110
level: high
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
    LogonType: 3 # Network Logon
  timeframe: 5m
  condition: selection | count(AccountName) by SourceNetworkAddress > 20
falsepositives:
  - Misconfigured services or legitimate users repeatedly failing to log in.
indicators.description: This rule detects a high number of failed network logins from a single source, indicating a potential brute-force attack against a management server, as suggested in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process of Web Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process of Web Server
id: a06a2f4d-3c8b-4e2d-bf0a-4b5c6d7e8f9a
status: experimental
description: Detects web server processes spawning shells or reverse shell clients, which may indicate a web application compromise.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-19
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/n-able-confirms-hackers-accessed-cloud.html
tags:
  - attack.t1059
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\tomcat.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\sh.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
      - '\netcat.exe'
      - '\nc.exe'
      - '\socat.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts or applications that spawn shells from a web server process.
indicators.description: This rule detects when a web server process spawns a command shell or common reverse shell tool, a strong indicator of compromise via a public-facing application.
